Of all the tickets printed for "Multiply Your Money", about half are still unsold. The game is near the midpoint of its run, with four of seven top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Today's free summary of "Multiply Your Money" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
805.headline: How much has sold

806.body:
About half of the tickets for "Win $50, $100 or $200" have been sold. The game is in the middle of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Today's free summary of "Win $50, $100 or $200" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
806.headline: How much has sold

807.body:
On "Ravens X2", one $20,000 top prize was claimed last week. That leaves two of the original four. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Today's free summary of "Ravens X2" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
807.headline: Another top prize was claimed

808.body:
"Ravens X10" is near the midpoint of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

Every line of Ravens X10's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
808.headline: How much has sold

809.body:
"Gold Bar Bingo" is down to five top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed in this morning's update. The game started with seven top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

Tomorrow's count on "Gold Bar Bingo" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
809.headline: The first top prize was claimed

810.body:
A $50,000 top prize on "In the Green" was claimed three days ago. The game started with seven top prizes and has five top prizes left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

If "In the Green" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
810.headline: Another top prize was claimed

811.body:
"Extreme Green" has gone close to two months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a third of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $1 million prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

If you play "Extreme Green" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
811.headline: No new top prize claims

812.body:
On "Loose Change®", one $1,000 top prize was claimed last week. That leaves fifteen of the original 24. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

The numbers for "Loose Change®" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
812.headline: Top prize count went down

813.body:
"The Price is Right™" has 407,826 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $5,000 prize, with eight left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Every line of The Price is Right™'s prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
813.headline: What's actually left to win

814.body:
One of High Voltage's top prizes was claimed three days ago. A player in Maryland won $100,000. The game started with eight top prizes and now has six top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

The numbers for "High Voltage" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
814.headline: Fewer $100,000 prizes left

815.body:
The prize money on "$100,000 Crossword" leans toward the smaller prizes. It is spread over eight prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $100,000. Games built like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

The numbers for "$100,000 Crossword" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
815.headline: What type of game it is

816.body:
On "Deluxe Crossword", one $50,000 top prize was claimed two weeks ago. That leaves seven of the original eight. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Everything above about "Deluxe Crossword" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
816.headline: A top prize was just claimed

817.body:
One of Hello Money!'s top prizes was claimed last week. A player in Maryland won $50,000. The game started with seven top prizes and now has six top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

The numbers for "Hello Money!" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.

819.headline: Tickets sold so far

820.body:
"Cozy Cash" just reached Maryland stores with 35 top prizes of $500. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the printed odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

The numbers for "Cozy Cash" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.

"Season's Greetings" is new from the Maryland Lottery. It is a $2 game with six top prizes of $10,000. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

If you play "Season's Greetings" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.

822.headline: New in stores

823.body:
"Holly-Day Cash" has joined the Maryland lineup at $5 with seven top prizes of $50,000. Only on the first day do the printed odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

The numbers for "Holly-Day Cash" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.

"Winter Multiplier" is new from the Maryland Lottery. It is a $10 game with nine top prizes of $100,000. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

The table below shows the full count for "Winter Multiplier", with every prize level included.
